findings.description: A static AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block. They are committed to version control, persisted in Terraform state, and readable in the AWS console/API by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration.

findings.issue_category: missing CMK encryption of environment variables
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables containing the secret material are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are returned in plaintext to anyone who can read the function configuration, with no separate key policy layer to constrain access.
The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past end of support and no longer receives security patches for the runtime or underlying OS image.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound network access and no security group boundary, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.
The assume-role policy trusts the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the trust is not scoped to a specific account or function ARN.
